Subject: RE: Question on prompt-state metering & billing during POC

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Below is the concise policy language you can paste into the SOW; I've also attached our updated ratecard and a short FAQ on prefix/prompt-state behavior.

Short policy summary (official):
- Full cache hit: If a request is served end-to-end from Redwood's prompt-state / prefix cache without invoking the model runtime (i.e., the cached response and outputs are returned directly), we only bill for outgoing/output tokens. Input tokens are not charged in this case because no model compute was performed.
- Partial (prefix) hit: If there is a partial KV cache hit and the request requires the model to generate tokens beyond the cached prefix, the customer is billed for the tokens actually processed by the runtime. Practically, that means you are charged for: (a) the uncached input tokens that hit the model plus (b) the generated output tokens. The cached portion is not billed separately.
- Cold-starts / warm-up: We recognize pilots create a high volume of cold misses. For pilots that convert to a committed plan within 90 days, Redwood offers a one-time warm-up credit that offsets billed tokens for the first N cold-start requests (we recommend specifying a token budget in the SOW).

Proposal for BrightMart pilot (suggested SOW language you can paste):
"Redwood will provide a warm-up credit equal to 250,000 input-token equivalents during the initial 60-day pilot. During this period, only billed tokens beyond this credit will be invoiced. Full cache hits continue to be billed only for output tokens as described in the Redwood Metering Policy."

Commercial options we recommend for production:
- Commit-based tiering (monthly): Discounted per-token rate once committed monthly spend reached.
- Tiered warm-cache exclusion: negotiate a sustained warm-cache exclusion for an agreed token volume if BrightMart commits to an annual reserved capacity.

I've attached redwood-ratecard-v2.xlsx which surfaces per-token rules and sample calculations for partial hits. The FAQ has three worked examples that mirror your pilot traffic patterns. If you want, Neha can run your sample-prod-traffic.csv through our estimator and produce a conservative spend projection.

Let me know if the SOW snippet works and whether you want a short call with procurement to walk them through the policy.

Cheers,
Markus
